title: Verdant Loop Software — EU POC Account Brief (CS working doc)
account_snapshot: Company: Verdant Loop Software (verdantloop.com) • Segment: mid-market • Industry: SaaS (product analytics) • HQ region: EU • Primary buyer/owner: Maya Patel • Sales stage (internal): evaluation → moving toward POC-in-flight.
products_in_scope: Interested products: Hosted API first (validate UX + integration), then Dedicated for predictable throughput/cost. Workloads discussed: chat, embeddings, reranking. Deployment requirements: public cloud + optional VPC.
use_cases: Primary use-cases remain: in-app support agent + doc search, plus personalization and summarization for product analytics workflows.
key_requirements_security_privacy: Security requirements captured so far: SSO (SAML), audit logging, KMS (key wrapping / customer-managed keys discussion), EU data residency for persisted artifacts (logs + embeddings). Compliance language requested: ISO27001 alignment (client mentioned ISO posture; may also ask about SOC 2 in procurement packet). Retention expectation: audit logs retained 1 year (client-side requirement).
data_residency_positioning: Verdant Loop statement (from calls): “EU data must reside in EU for persisted logs and embeddings.” They are willing to allow ephemeral inference routing outside the EU only if (a) no persistence and (b) contract wording is explicit. Legal flagged: “cannot store tokens outside EU without explicit consent.”
latency_throughput_targets: Updated technical targets (most recent): p95 chat latency <300ms in EU-primary (earlier ask was <250ms; they relaxed target slightly after discussing streaming + network variance). Peak throughput estimate still ~80 req/s per region during incidents; normal load lower. Degraded mode: cross-region failover acceptable if p95 stays <600ms and residency for persisted artifacts is preserved.
routing_requirements: Multi-region routing requirement remains: EU-primary with soft failover to NA for availability/DR. Routing policy must preserve EU residency for persisted artifacts (embeddings/logs). They want explicit metrics and a clear explanation of what is “ephemeral” vs “persisted” in our system.
model_preferences: Preference remains for open model families. Earlier mentions: Llama-2-Chat and Mistral. Newer testing ask: prioritize Llama-3 Instruct + Mistral (current-gen) for quality; they’re open to 4-bit quantized variants on Dedicated if quality is acceptable. They want a cost-sensitive route option (smaller model) for low-risk queries.
poc_scope_current: POC is now planned as ~45 days (was 30 days) to accommodate legal review + security testing. Region: EU-west. Traffic: synthetic + replayed traces. Goals: validate latency/throughput targets, SSO (SAML) integration, KMS encryption test, and compare hosted vs dedicated cost/perf. Volume placeholder: ~150k tokens/month equivalent for test harness (up from ~100k in the initial scope).
pricing_and_packaging_notes: They requested a clean pricing table covering (1) Hosted baseline and (2) Dedicated reserved pricing with 1/3/6 GPU size options. They remain cost-sensitive and want clear explanation of price delta drivers (infra, isolation, reserved capacity). Expect pushback if Dedicated delta is not justified by measurable latency stability and predictable spend.
blockers: 1) Legal signoff on EU data residency addendum (still the main gating item). 2) Clarify EU multi-region routing SLOs (especially failover behavior and what gets persisted where). 3) Pricing clarity: Dedicated vs Hosted delta and what each includes (support/SLA, isolation, VPC options).
next_steps_2_weeks: 1) Send updated EU-region SLA + data residency addendum draft for Verdant Loop redlines. 2) Schedule infra runthrough + routing deep dive with their platform lead (target week of 2026-03-24). 3) Provide updated pricing table + node sizing recommendations (1/3/6 GPU) with assumptions. 4) Share latency benchmark report in EU-west (include streaming vs non-streaming, batching/KV cache guidance).

risks_and_watchouts: Risk: procurement/legal stalls if residency language is not unambiguous. Risk: expectation mismatch on failover (they want availability, but also strict residency for persisted data). Risk: if Dedicated pricing delta is large, they may remain Hosted-only or evaluate alternatives.
internal_owner_notes: CS focus: keep legal + security momentum; ensure we deliver a single crisp narrative on residency + routing. SE focus: provide EU-west benchmarks and clear recommended configs (batching/KV cache) to hit latency targets without overspending. Sales focus: simplify pricing story and tie Dedicated value to measurable SLO stability.
